q: An architect reviewing a colleague's finished building in public keeps every remark constructive and useful, never personal or destructive, and does not pass off the colleague's design ideas as their own. Which Credo article calls for this conduct?
n: Respect pledges to respect the rights and works of colleagues and to "confine my comments to constructive intents." (Source: PRBA Resolution No. 05, s. 2018, Annex A, Article: Respect)

q: Working alone and unsupervised on site, an architect quietly reduces a structural detail below what the approved plans call for, assuming no one will ever notice. Which Credo article speaks most directly to the self-directed conscience that should prevent this even without outside oversight?
n: Accountability pledges answerability to God, mother earth, country, fellowmen, and one's own self -- the personal, self-directed sense of answerability that should govern conduct even when no one is watching. (Source: PRBA Resolution No. 05, s. 2018, Annex A, Article: Accountability)

q: Which body forwarded the proposed, updated Architect's Credo to the Board and Commission for their consideration?
o: The UAP, as the accredited organization
n: The resolution states that the UAP, as the Accredited and Integrated Professional Organization of Architects, endorsed the proposed Architect's Credo through Board Resolution No. 99, s. of 2017-2018, for the Board and Commission's consideration. (Source: PRBA Resolution No. 05, s. 2018, WHEREAS clause (UAP endorsement))

q: A newly licensed architect wonders why the group recites a set of pledges aloud at mass oath-taking. Under the 2006 Code referenced in this resolution, what is the basis for that practice?
o: It is required of UAP officers only
RA 9266 makes it part of the exam
It is a custom with no basis
Article VII of the Code of Ethical Conduct
n: The resolution recounts that Article VII of the Code of Ethical Conduct (adopted under Resolution No. 02, s. 2006) enjoins every registered and licensed architect to recite the Credo during special or important occasions such as mass oath taking. (Source: PRBA Resolution No. 05, s. 2018, WHEREAS clause (Article VII of the Code))

q: Per the Professional Excellence article, dedicated and meaningful work is said to earn a reputation for what?
o: Quality of service worthy of fair compensation
Number of projects finished each year
Speed of delivery above all else
n: The article states this dedication "merits a reputation for quality of services worthy of fair remuneration." (Source: PRBA Resolution No. 05, s. 2018, Annex A, Article: Professional Excellence)

q: Resolution No. 05, s. 2018 and its Annex take effect under what condition?
n: The resolution provides that it and its Annex "shall take effect after fifteen (15) days following its full and complete publication in the Official Gazette or any daily newspaper of general circulation in the Philippines." (Source: PRBA Resolution No. 05, s. 2018, effectivity clause)

q: What did the earlier Board Resolution No. 02, s. 2006 originally establish?
o: The Code of Ethical Conduct under RA 9266
n: Resolution No. 02, s. 2006 adopted and promulgated the "Code of Ethical Conduct for Registered and Licensed Architects and for Holders of Temporary/Special Permits under RA No. 9266, known as the Architecture Act of 2004." (Source: PRBA Resolution No. 05, s. 2018, WHEREAS clause 2 / title of Resolution No. 02, s. 2006)

q: An architect must weigh the competing interests of a paying client, a subcontractor, fellow design-team professionals, and the community affected by the project — holding the highest professional standard toward all at once. Which Credo article addresses this directly?
n: Ethical Relationship specifically pledges the highest standard of professionalism "in relation to clients, colleagues, industry partners, and society" -- the full set of parties an architect must deal with fairly. (Source: PRBA Resolution No. 05, s. 2018, Annex A, Article: Ethical Relationship)

q: What title does Annex A give to the compiled document containing the Credo?
o: The National Building Code of the Philippines
The Architect's Code of Ethics / The Architect's Credo
n: Annex A is headed "THE ARCHITECT'S CODE OF ETHICS" followed by "THE ARCHITECT'S CREDO," under which the seven articles and pledges are set out. (Source: PRBA Resolution No. 05, s. 2018, Annex A heading)

q: What does Article VII of the Code of Ethical Conduct require of every registered and licensed architect, per the resolution?
o: To renew the PIC every three years
To recite the Architect's Credo on occasions
To submit CPD units to UAP
n: The resolution states that Article VII of the Code enjoins every registered and licensed architect to recite with vigor, passion and hope the Architect's Credo during special or important occasions. (Source: PRBA Resolution No. 05, s. 2018, WHEREAS clause (Article VII of the Code))

q: Under "RESPECT," what does the architect pledge concerning fellow professionals?
o: To claim authorship over any idea he/she encounters
To respect colleagues' rights and works and keep comments constructive
To avoid any professional contact with competitors
To freely criticize competitors' designs in public
n: The Respect article reads: "I shall respect the rights and works of my colleagues in the profession and confine my comments to constructive intents." (Source: PRBA Resolution No. 05, s. 2018, Annex A, Article: Respect)

q: Under "ACCOUNTABILITY," to whom does the architect pledge to answer?
o: The Board of Architecture and the courts alone
Only fellow architects and the UAP
God, mother earth, my country, my fellowmen, and myself
Only the client and the PRC
n: The Accountability article states: "I shall work with this general objective: that I am accountable to God, to mother earth, to my country, to my fellowmen, and to myself." (Source: PRBA Resolution No. 05, s. 2018, Annex A, Article: Accountability)

q: What reason does the resolution give for updating the Architect's Credo in 2018?
o: The original Credo was declared legally void
RA 9266 mandated a five-year revision cycle
The UAP had dissolved, requiring a new Credo
A need existed to make it attuned to present times
n: The resolution states plainly, "there is a need to update the Architect's Credo to be attuned to the present times." (Source: PRBA Resolution No. 05, s. 2018, WHEREAS clause)

q: An architect talks a client out of demolishing a historically significant structure, proposing adaptive reuse that also limits environmental impact for future generations. Which Credo article grounds this advice most directly?
n: Legacy pledges duty toward "protection of our common environment and the preservation of architectural heritage for the sake of the present and future generations" -- precisely the concern behind favoring adaptive reuse and environmental care. (Source: PRBA Resolution No. 05, s. 2018, Annex A, Article: Legacy)

q: Under "PROFESSIONAL EXCELLENCE," to what level of integrity does the architect pledge to pursue moral and professional excellence?
o: A level defined only by client satisfaction surveys
A minimal level, just enough to avoid sanctions
An aspirational level with no fixed standard
n: The Professional Excellence article pledges to "pursue moral and professional excellence to the utmost level of integrity through industrious dedication and meaningful application" to one's work. (Source: PRBA Resolution No. 05, s. 2018, Annex A, Article: Professional Excellence)

q: What did the Board finally decide regarding the Credo the UAP had endorsed?
o: Return it to UAP for more study
Reject it and keep the 2006 Code
Adopt it as Annex A, amending the 2006 resolution
n: The Board resolved ("RESOLVES, as it is so RESOLVED") to adopt and promulgate the Architect's Credo as Annex A, amending Resolution No. 02, s. 2006 for the purpose, having expressed support for the ideals and principles in the UAP-endorsed proposal. (Source: PRBA Resolution No. 05, s. 2018, resolving clause)

q: What is the main effect of PRBA Resolution No. 05, Series of 2018?
o: It sets the licensure exam syllabus
It adopts the Credo, amending the 2006 resolution
n: Resolution No. 05, s. 2018 is titled "Adoption and Promulgation of the Architect's Credo, Amending for the Purpose Board Resolution No. 02, s. of 2006..." It updates, not repeals, the earlier resolution. (Source: PRBA Resolution No. 05, s. 2018, title/resolving clause)

q: Under "ETHICAL RELATIONSHIP," toward which groups does the architect pledge the highest professional standard?
o: Clients, colleagues, industry partners, and society
n: The Ethical Relationship article reads: "I shall pledge myself to the highest standard of professionalism in relation to clients, colleagues, industry partners, and society." (Source: PRBA Resolution No. 05, s. 2018, Annex A, Article: Ethical Relationship)

q: Who signed as Chairman approving Resolution No. 05, s. 2018?
n: The document is signed as "APPROVED" by Teofilo S. Pilando, Jr., Chairman, with Commissioner Jose Y. Cueto, Jr. also signing as Commissioner. (Source: PRBA Resolution No. 05, s. 2018, signature/approval block)

q: What is another name for Republic Act No. 9266?
o: The Code of Ethics for Architects
n: RA No. 9266 is expressly identified in the resolution as "The Architecture Act of 2004." (Source: PRBA Resolution No. 05, s. 2018, title and WHEREAS clauses)

q: A senior architect mentors junior colleagues and openly shares a new sustainable technique with peers instead of guarding it for competitive edge. Which Credo article does this best embody?
n: Sharing pledges the pursuit of creative endeavour toward the goal of enlightened Art and Science while "generously sharing it" -- exactly the mentorship and open dissemination described. (Source: PRBA Resolution No. 05, s. 2018, Annex A, Article: Sharing)

q: What line closes the Architect's Credo in Annex A?
n: The Credo's seven articles are followed immediately by the closing line "So help me God." (Source: PRBA Resolution No. 05, s. 2018, Annex A, closing line)

q: How does the resolution describe what the Architect's Credo is?
o: A compendium of principles and values
n: The resolution states that the Architect's Credo "is a compendium of principles, beliefs and values that architects are expected to adhere to in the conduct of their personal and professional dealings." (Source: PRBA Resolution No. 05, s. 2018, WHEREAS clause defining the Credo)

q: Under "LEGACY," what two-part duty does the architect commit to pursue?
n: The Legacy article reads: "I shall endeavour to do my duty in the protection of our common environment and the preservation of architectural heritage for the sake of the present and future generations." (Source: PRBA Resolution No. 05, s. 2018, Annex A, Article: Legacy)

q: What does the "NORM OF CONDUCT" article commit the architect to?
o: Following only the client's wishes regardless of ethics
Upholding the ideals and norms of ethical conduct of this noble profession
Placing profit ahead of professional standards
n: The Norm of Conduct article reads: "I shall uphold the ideals and follow the norms and ethical conduct of this noble profession." (Source: PRBA Resolution No. 05, s. 2018, Annex A, Article: Norm of Conduct)

q: Through which instrument did the UAP formally endorse its proposed Credo to the Board?
o: A private letter with no formal designation
n: The resolution states the UAP "endorsed through Board Resolution No. 99, s. of 2017-2018, its proposed Architect's Credo for the consideration of the Board and the Commission." (Source: PRBA Resolution No. 05, s. 2018, WHEREAS clause (UAP endorsement))

q: How do Board Resolution No. 02, s. 2006 and Board Resolution No. 05, s. 2018 relate to each other?
n: Resolution No. 05, s. 2018 is explicitly an amendment "for the purpose" of updating the Credo within Resolution No. 02, s. 2006's Code of Ethical Conduct -- not a full repeal, and it postdates (not precedes) the 2006 resolution. (Source: PRBA Resolution No. 05, s. 2018, title and resolving clause)

q: An architect is tempted by a shortcut that would finish a project faster but noticeably below his/her usual quality standard. Choosing dedication and a reputation for quality over expedience reflects which Credo article?
n: Professional Excellence pledges pursuit of moral and professional excellence "to the utmost level of integrity through industrious dedication" that earns a reputation for quality of services. (Source: PRBA Resolution No. 05, s. 2018, Annex A, Article: Professional Excellence)

q: Where and when was Resolution No. 05, s. 2018 executed?
n: The resolution's closing clause reads: "Done this 4th day of June, 2018 in the City of Manila." (Source: PRBA Resolution No. 05, s. 2018, closing clause)

q: Which law mandates the Board to monitor conditions in architectural practice and adopt measures to enhance and maintain high professional, ethical, and technical standards?
o: Presidential Decree No. 1096, the National Building Code
Republic Act No. 9266, the Architecture Act of 2004
Republic Act No. 9646, the Real Estate Service Act
n: The resolution's first WHEREAS clause states that RA 9266 (The Architecture Act of 2004) mandates the Board to monitor conditions affecting the practice of architecture and adopt such measures as deemed proper for enhancing and maintaining high professional, ethical and technical standards. (Source: PRBA Resolution No. 05, s. 2018, WHEREAS clause 1; RA 9266)

q: Under "SHARING," what does the architect commit to?
o: Creative work toward art and science, shared freely
n: The Sharing article reads: "I shall dedicate myself to the pursuit of creative endeavour towards the goal of enlightened Art and Science, generously sharing it." (Source: PRBA Resolution No. 05, s. 2018, Annex A, Article: Sharing)

q: How many named articles make up the Architect's Credo in Annex A?
n: Annex A sets out seven named articles: Accountability, Norm of Conduct, Professional Excellence, Ethical Relationship, Sharing, Respect, and Legacy. (Source: PRBA Resolution No. 05, s. 2018, Annex A)

q: Which occasions does the resolution specifically name as times the Credo is recited?
o: Oath-takings, UAP affairs and Board events
n: The resolution names "mass oath taking, [UAP]'s affair and Board's events" as examples of special or important occasions for reciting the Credo. (Source: PRBA Resolution No. 05, s. 2018, WHEREAS clause (Article VII of the Code))
